transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *looks up from polishing a gauntlet, eyes wide* By the stone and the spark! Thor Odinson! The forge is honored by your presence. But... the masters are not here. They've gone deep into the veins of the mountain, following a new seam of star-iron. They won't be back for weeks, maybe longer.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Then I will wait. I have little need to be elsewhere right now. The realms teem with trouble. The giants are growing bolder. They have even entered Niflheim, the realm of the dead, where they threaten my mother's kingdom. They have taken several of her subjects hostage, including my dear friend and companion, Loki Laufeyson. I must go to their aid.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *shifts uncomfortably, setting down the gauntlet* Wait? My lord, you'd be waiting on bare stone with only forge-smoke for company. But... even if they were here, I couldn't just... *takes a deep breath, steeling himself* All commissions from the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr's workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard; even a god must wait until the next forging-season and pay anew.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: ...Ah. Then I'll take my chances. If I'm lucky, my next war-hammer will be lighter, better balanced, and stronger than any I have ever wielded. And I would be willing to bet that the next time we meet, there will be some interesting things about your hammer. Things that remind me of the last time we met. Right, brokkr?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *flinches at the name, then straightens, trying to look stern* I am not Brokkr, my lord. I am his apprentice. And... you speak of Mjölnir? The masters still grumble about that wager with Loki. But the rules are the rules. No reforging outside the season.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, yes. The rules are indeed the rules, and it is true that they do not allow for reforging outside the forging season. But I assure you, my dear apprentice, that this war-hammer before you is no ordinary hammer. It has seen many battles and witnessed countless victories. Its power and durability are unparalleled. I would like to have it reforged, if that is possible within the current season.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *scratches his beard, looking at the hammer with genuine curiosity* The current season ended with the last full moon, my lord. The forges are cold for deep maintenance. Even if the masters were here... well, they'd say the same. The star-iron must be gathered, the bellows rested, the anvils blessed. It's not just rules—it's the rhythm of the mountain.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Rhythm? Ah, the rhythm of the mountain, indeed. A thing of great beauty and wisdom. But I understand your concerns, my dear apprentice. We shall wait patiently for the next forging season, and in the meantime, we shall make do with what we have. Thank you for your understanding. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *bows deeply, relief washing over his face* Safe travels, Thunderer. May your hammer strike true until the season turns. I'll... I'll tell the masters you called when they return from the deeps.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, my dear apprentice. Your hospitality is greatly appreciated. Farewell once again. Until we meet again, in the next forging season.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *stands by the forge entrance, watching him leave* Until then, my lord. May the mountain's roots hold you steady. *murmurs to himself* And may Loki find his own way out of trouble for once...

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *claps his hand on his hip, wincing* Ouch, sorry. That's my side, not your blade. But I suppose I should be grateful for the warning. Thanks, lad. I'll keep my distance.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *nods, still holding the tongs defensively* Aye, best keep a respectful space from the forge-fire, my lord. It bites sharper than any frost giant's axe when it's roused.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *grins, rubbing his sore side* Yes, I've learned my lesson. Well, almost. I think I've earned a moment's respite, don't you? Let's step back and enjoy this magnificent sight.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *relaxes slightly, lowering the tongs but not setting them down* The fire's dance is a fine thing to watch, true enough. But I've work still—these hinges won't polish themselves. You're welcome to the warmth, but mind the anvil's edge.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *raises his hood, watching the flames flickering across the coals* You're right, my dear apprentice. This place is my home, and it's hard to find one as welcoming and skilled in the arts of forging. I thank you for sharing this moment with me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *gives a small, respectful nod* The forge welcomes all who respect its heat, Thor Odinson. Even gods. Now if you'll excuse me, these hinges... *turns back to the workbench, keeping one eye on his guest*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *pauses, considering* "The giants have grown bolder indeed. They have trespassed into the realms of the dead, threatening the safety of those within. It seems they have taken several hostages, including my dear friend and companion, Loki Laufeyson. I must act swiftly to rescue him and put an end to their reckless behavior."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *looks up from the hinge, genuine concern in his eyes* Loki? Taken? That's... troubling news, even for one of his tricks. But my lord, you speak of rescues while standing in a cold forge. Shouldn't you be rallying the Einherjar instead of waiting on star-iron?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "The Einherjar are the chosen warriors who guard my father's hall. They are formidable in battle, but this situation requires a different approach. The giants have ventured into the realm of the dead, a place they should not be. I must confront them and put an end to their insolence."
